newsitem.title: UK: Euro low sulph straight-run fuel boosted by crude.
newsitem.headline: Euro low sulph straight-run fuel boosted by crude.

text.p: Low sulphur straight-run fuel gained again in Europe on Wednesday on a scarcity of supply and the underlying surge in crude prices, traders said.
A cargo of 0.8 percent material moved privately late on Tuesday from an ARA refiner but it was unclear if it had gone into the barge market as reported.
The next available cargo, not due till third decade August, was on offer at $113-$114 a tonne before crude's hike in price and then at $114-$115 later.
Traders doubted such numbers were realistic and pegged values at $110/$113 a tonne.
But high sulphur Russian values were slipping, with supply growing because the U.S. arb window is closed and last week's buying fever has abated.
More E4 cargoes were looming on the horizon and values were pegged at three means plus $3 or $4, while straight-run M100 was on offer around two means plus $3-$5.
